Summary: Arianism taught in the early 4th century that the Son of God was created by the Father and therefore not eternal or fully God. It held that there was a time when the Son did not exist.
Beliefs: Jesus Christ was created by God the Father; The Son is not eternal; The Son is divine but not fully God; The Father alone is uncreated
Controversy: Condemned at the Council of Nicaea AD 325, which produced the Nicene Creed
ChristianResponse: The church affirmed that the Son is of one substance with the Father and eternally begotten, not made, citing John 1:1 and Colossians 1:15-17.
